content: Candidiasis is a condition that arises when the yeast _Candida_, which is normally present in certain parts of the body, grows uncontrollably. The symptoms of candidiasis vary depending on the specific type of infection. These include vaginal candidiasis, oral candidiasis, esophageal candidiasis, or invasive candidiasis. Healthcare professionals use different diagnostic tests to identify candidiasis, and the choice of test depends on the type of infection being evaluated. Certain factors increase the risk of developing candidiasis. These include having a compromised immune system and the use of antibiotics. There are specific strategies to prevent the various types of candidiasis, which individuals can learn and implement. The treatment of candidiasis involves the use of antifungal medications. The choice of antifungal, its dosage, and the method of administration depend on the type of infection. Invasive candidiasis is a severe form of the condition. Clinical information is available regarding its characteristics, methods of prevention, diagnostic testing, and treatment options. Candidemia, the most prevalent form of invasive candidiasis, has been studied extensively, and data on its trends are available. The incidence of antifungal-resistant invasive candidiasis is on the rise, and there are limited antifungal treatment options available to address this growing concern. Globally, fungal diseases and antifungal resistance are becoming more prevalent. Misdiagnosis of fungal infections is a common issue. Educational and communication materials, such as social media graphics, fact sheets, infographics, and animated videos, are available for public and professional use. Webinars, podcasts, and clinical tools featuring leading experts in fungal diseases are accessible, providing valuable resources for healthcare professionals.
